author: edwong57
body:
Dear all,

As part of https://github.com/geneontology/go-ontology/issues/32256, GO:0035037 sperm entry is being moved out of endocytosis. It is now a child of GO:0022412 cellular process involved in reproduction in multicellular organism, and it remains part_of GO:0007338 single fertilization.

GO:0035037 | sperm entry
Definition: "A process that results in penetration of the egg shell through the micropyle (a specialized anterior opening in the vitelline envelope) and entry of the entire sperm, including the surrounding plasma membrane and the sperm tail, into the egg cytoplasm. This step in fertilization is seen in Drosophila, where a plasma membrane fusion event between the sperm and the egg does not occur." [PMID:9630751]

The term describes Drosophila micropylar sperm entry. None of the current annotations is from Drosophila, and neither the mouse nor the worm data describe this mechanism, so the annotations should be moved.

| Group | Gene | Evidence | Reference | Claude analysis suggestion |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MGI | Ube3a (MGI:105098) | IMP | PMID:11756548 | The data come from a sperm penetration assay with zona-free hamster oocytes (sperm capacitation index; Table 2), which measures mammalian sperm-egg interaction rather than micropylar entry. The authors attribute the effect to E6-AP's steroid receptor coactivator role. Suggest GO:0007338 single fertilization. |
| WB | spe-38 (WBGene00013121) | IMP | PMID:15930110 | spe-38 sperm contact oocytes but fail to fertilize them. spe-38 already has GO:0007338 single fertilization (IMP) from the same paper, so suggest removing this annotation. If the paper shows whether binding or fusion fails, GO:0035036 sperm-egg recognition or GO:0007342 fusion of sperm to egg plasma membrane involved in single fertilization would be more specific. |

Impacted groups:

| Group | EXP |
|---|---|
| MGI | 1 |
| WB | 1 |


** Group contacts: https://github.com/geneontology/go-site/blob/master/metadata/group-contacts.csv

Thanks.
